title: Vickers Wellington R1028
memorial_details: description: IN MEMORIAM.  THIS MEMORIAL PLAQUE IS INSTALLED IN HONOUR OF THE FIVE AIRCREW WHO LOST THEIR LIVES IN THE CRASH OF WELLINGTON BOMBER R1028 ON THE NIGHT OF 7 OCTOBER 1943.  THE AIRCRAFT, ON FINAL APPROACH TO LITTLE RISSINGTON, CRASHED IN THE BACK GARDEN OF THE LAMB INN.  THE ONLY SURVIVOR WAS THE REAR GUNNER, SERGEANT JOHN SMITH, WHO HAD THIS PLAQUE INSTALLED WITH THE KIND PERMISSION OF THE LAMB INN OWNER, MR CLEVERLEY.  THE NAMES OF THE CREW MEMBERS WHO DIED ARE LISTED AS FOLLOWS: FLIGHT SERGEANT JACK A HAZELDENE, PILOT, RAF.  BURIED AT ST PETER'S CHURCHYARD, LITTLE RISSINGTON.  SERGEANT W. A. JONES, NAVIGATOR, SERGEANT J. V. REES, BOMB AIMER, SERGEANT J. A. JOHNSON, W/OP, SERGEANT H. COOK, SECOND NAVIGATOR. THAT THEY BE NOT FORGOTTEN, NO 21 OTU, RAF BOMBER COMMAND.  PER ARDUA AD ASTRA.  BY SERGEANT SMITH EX RAF, VANCOUVER, CANADA, 1988.'
inscription: A BRONZE ON WOOD PLAQUE, PROPELLOR BLADE AND PHOTOGRAPHS OF CREW MEMBERS, ALL HUNG ON A WALL OF THE PUB.
